Let's talk about pest, I present to you, African Land Snail.
Escargo. Nevermind, evidently snails caught in the wild are considered a health risk.

In Hawaii, slugs and snails may sometimes eat rat dropping and become vectors for rat lung worm disease. The primary vector for the disease is a another species of pseudo snail but in general, we must very careful about controlling our mollusk here.

Understanding pest is just as important as understanding your seeds and soil.

This is the African Land Snail with a quarter for scale. They are an invasive species on the Big Island of Hawaii and are a night mare to deal with.

Challenges of controlling this pest:

  • They can climp tall barriers.
  • They are too big to fit in most beer traps.
  • They can eat a lot of slug bait and not die
  • They move fast enough to brave coffee grind barriers.
  • It only takes one to destroy a small garden in an evening
  • They are nocturnal and Hawaii has no insectivores that regularly prays on them.
  • They are a potential vector for rat-lungworm disease.

They tend to hide under leaf litter during the day but have difficulty burrowing unlike slugs so they are easy to locate and remove. I feed them to the birds.

An interesting thing I discovered about them is that will indiscriminately target green plant matter. I used to have a bed bordered with green onions and the snails would always attack it and get sick but couldn't make into the rest of the patch.

That's all for now, fam.
